headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared content handling; no direct filesystem or MCP bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests customer-support documents, personal data, and workflows, while Dagster orchestrates data pipelines. A plausible pathway exists if Cognee outputs are fed into Dagster assets or metadata without provenance checks. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty remains, but the pairwise interaction is enough to keep this above low.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into Dagster pipeline definitions or metadata without validation, prompt injection can propagate.
IF a shared workspace or message channel is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Cognee outputs before Dagster consumes them.
Require manual review of any text that becomes Dagster config or metadata.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from imported documents before indexing.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data and finance data, and its network egress is allowlisted. Dagster has no filesystem or network egress in its profile, so the main leakage path is Cognee exporting sensitive content to external services during processing. The pairwise risk is medium because sensitive data is present, but Dagster itself does not add an outbound leak path.
conditions: IF Cognee sends indexed customer-support or finance data to an allowlisted third-party API, leakage occurs.
IF Dagster is configured to pass sensitive payloads into Cognee jobs, those payloads may be exposed to Cognee's inference backend.
mitigations: Restrict Cognee inputs to non-sensitive subsets.
Review the allowlist for external endpoints.
Disable sensitive-data indexing for finance and personal data.
Use redaction before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, while Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is little direct write overlap, so conflict is limited. The only plausible contention is shared upstream resources or session-level state, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource, their updates can race.
IF an orchestrator adds shared write access not shown in the profiles, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Avoid shared mutable git or filesystem targets.
Use per-session identifiers for Cognee runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator, so if it consumes Cognee outputs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream pipeline actions. Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and schema structures, which Dagster could operationalize. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Dagster treats Cognee-generated decisions or schemas as authoritative, downstream actions can propagate errors.
IF a verification gate is inserted before Dagster execution, the cascade is reduced.
mitigations: Require human approval for Cognee-derived changes.
Validate schemas before orchestration.
Log and diff all upstream outputs.
Limit Dagster to read-only preview mode for Cognee inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated verification and rollback gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and customer-support data, while Dagster's profile does not show matching compliance controls or residency guarantees. Because the pair may move regulated data through Cognee into orchestration workflows, the mismatch is a compliance concern. Dagster is not cited for a specific violation because its compliance posture is undocumented.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support or finance data is routed through Cognee into Dagster workflows, compliance obligations apply.
IF Dagster is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from Cognee's handling, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Classify regulated datasets before routing.
Keep PHI out of the pair entirely.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Review residency and DPA requirements.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
